notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 20% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Pavel Mintyukov is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Drew Helleson has taken his spot beside Travis Mitchell.
Travis Mitchell was added to the roster on Oct 30 and has played beside Pavel Mintyukov.
Roger McQueen was added to the roster on Oct 30 and has played beside Alex Killorn and Nikita Nesterenko.

Samuel Honzek is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Matt Coronato has taken his spot beside Mikael Backlund and Joel Farabee.
Joel Hanley has not dressed for the last 11 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jake Middleton has taken his spot beside Zayne Parekh.
Connor Zary is out (knee surgery) and has missed the last 10 games.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Maxim Tsyplakov returned in their last game after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Ben Jones was added to the roster on Oct 21 and has played beside Joel Farabee and Matt Coronato.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, up from 2% last season.

CGY.head: A slightly uphill night for the Flames
CGY.body: Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but Calgary has home-ice advantage, and the Ducks will be without Terry. The Flames’ best way to tip it is piling up shots.

ANA.head: The Ducks start a half-step ahead

story.head: The Flames come in rested
paras: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Ducks (5-7-1) lost 7-6 to Buffalo on Oct 29, while the Flames (6-7-0) beat Seattle 6-2 on Oct 30. The Ducks played last night, and the Flames are rested. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Ducks sixth (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Flames fifth (tied for 24th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Ducks hit a lot (4th) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (30th). Anaheim has allowed 3.85 goals a game, the second most in the league. As for the Flames, they do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest) and take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd). The Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Ducks. Beyond that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Leo Carlsson (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 13 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring, with nine points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Calgary. Beckett Sennecke (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Matvei Gridin (5 G / 5 A / 10 P in 13 GP) has a team-high five goals, with seven points in his last five games.

Ville Husso (1-3-0 / .858 SV% in 4 GS) has struggled for Anaheim so far, but will likely start. Dustin Wolf (2-4-0 / .848 SV% in 6 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Calgary, but will likely start.
At home, Ryan Huska likes to send Farabee, Backlund and Coronato out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Caulfield, Carlsson and Gauthier.
